match_id: GLASNER: “IT’S NOT ROCKET SCIENCE FOOTBALL!”  Crystal Palace_Everton_2026-05-10_rQ1CYmG6Yfg
team: GLASNER: “IT’S NOT ROCKET SCIENCE FOOTBALL!”  Crystal Palace
speaker: Head Coach
quote_text:
Okay, who'd like to start?  
Anybody? Oliver, pleased with the way you came  back from going behind twice? Yes, absolutely  
pleased with the performance. In the first 10  minutes, I told the players at half-time we  
could see the difference between Conference League  and Premier League. Conference League is also very  
technical, but Premier League is so physical.  And we were 1-0 down. It looked like a déjà vu  
from the Bournemouth game. Corner, near post,  conceding. Of course we talked about it, but the  
reaction was great, to be honest. Then we came  back into the game, I think played well, scored an  
amazing goal. And second half, almost the same. So  there was no chance, but then making one mistake  
and we are 2-1 down. And then when you have had  a game three days ago, playing against Everton,  
who are really playing very well, defending very  well, and everybody knows when they defend in a  
deep block, it is not so easy to create chances  against them. But then the way we played, the way  
we created chances, the commitment, the desire,  the confidence, the determination we had to play  
forward, to create chances, to score a goal, was  awesome for me. And at the end, fully deserved.  
And for me, then the reaction I loved. And it is  not now, okay, taking a breath, it is 2-2, saved  
the point. It was, okay, let’s go for the win.  And at the end it felt like Everton had played  
three days ago because we looked fresher, and that  is huge credit to the players. It is interesting  
you talk about your team looking fresher because  obviously last week you spoke about the mental  
fatigue. They did not look mentally fatigued or  really, apart from moments, physically fatigued.  
Do you think that partly was because of the  momentum and the excitement of Thursday night,  
getting to the Conference League final? Why do  you think that was? Yeah, I think the difference  
is the Bournemouth game was between the two  semi-finals. Let’s say the job in the Conference  
League was not done, whereas now we have two and a  half weeks’ time. So the final is so far away, and  
in our schedule it was our 56th game, I think, of  the season. In our schedule, two and a half weeks  
feels like eternity, so we do not think about it  and talk about it. And also right now, we have  
not to prepare for City, not for Vallecano, and  this was the opposite. This was different to the  
Bournemouth game. We knew it was just half-time.  We also had the travelling and, honestly,  
the players looked much better yesterday. That  is why I also decided not to rotate a lot. It was  
just the strikers, and Yeremy Pino was sick, so  that is why he was not involved in today’s game.  
But I think it was a little bit different. And I  also told the players, because this is, I think,  
also the development. For example, I remember when  we played Everton away with an excellent first 60  
minutes, but then we dropped off and we had also  a Thursday night game. We were physically fatigued  
and today it was the opposite. And I think this  is just the development and the progression the  
team made. When we are talking about dealing  with situations, using the experience to learn,  
I think today was evidence that the team is really  learning. But on the other side, in three days we  
have to go again. But this performance today will  help us to play a great game at the City Ground.  
A point obviously means you are that much closer,  that little bit closer to Premier League safety.  
Has there been any sort of nagging concern in  the back of your mind or the players’ minds at  
all about getting to that point? And if West Ham  do not win tonight, then you will be safe. Would  
that help going forward as well, do you think?  We said we want to make the Premier League clear,  
is it right, this Sunday with a win? That is why  we wanted to win, because we never want to depend  
on somebody else. We always want to decide it  ourselves. And this was the way we played and this  
is what I liked. And now let’s see how the game is  going. But to be honest, if we play like we played  
today, we will make enough points to stay in the  league, even when we play City and Arsenal and  
at Brentford. So it is maybe not the easiest games  to play, but we have shown that we are competitive  
against any team if we have this mentality, if we  have this spirit, and if we have this commitment  
to the game. And so that is why, at the end, yes,  we are talking about it, but we will get enough  
points, definitely. But there was an incident  at the end of the first half. It looked like a  
penalty should have been given to Crystal Palace.  What were your views on that? And with Jørgen?  
Yes. And did you have a few words with David  Moyes about that incident? I saw. No. David and I,  
we are even. David is a bit older than I, but we  said in the dugout, we are old school. The referee  
had a few too soft decisions, but on both sides.  So I watched it back. João showed it to me and,  
to be honest, it should not be a penalty. So in  the Premier League, no, I think it is what the  
Premier League is really famous for. And yeah,  it was a push, but again, these sort of pushes  
you have in every set play so often. So I think  it would have helped us, but I think it was okay.  
Thanks. Oliver, you said in your programme  notes that Everton were a formidable opponent.  
How satisfied were you that you were able to  adapt from the Conference League requirements  
on Thursday to a very different test today, and  coming back twice? Yes, very, very pleased and  
very proud of the players. I told them afterwards  because this is sport. You can win and lose,  
but the approach to a game, the way you play, the  confidence you have, the style. I think today, and  
we are always talking about we want to show our  style of play and we want to show our personality,  
and I have seen it today in the entire game.  Struggling a little bit coming into the game,  
finding the switch, but then adapting quickly  and then playing our game, and also accepting the  
strengths of Everton. They are good in set plays.  They just scored against City, where everybody is  
preparing. They are just doing great deliveries  and they are physically so strong, and they have  
a lot of belief in what they are doing. Then they  go quite direct forward also when Pickford plays  
the long balls, and they are strong. And then it  is okay, we have to compete. On the other side,  
our first goal was the same. They pressed us  higher, we went long and Jørgen Strand Larsen  
wins the duel. We pick up the second ball and then  we play and score a nice goal. So sometimes it  
is not rocket science football. It is just do the  basics right, and I think we did the basics right  
and also played some good football. But Everton,  on the other side as well, they were also always  
threatening. So when we made one or two mistakes,  at the end they had one or two good transitions,  
but overall it was a very good performance. Yeah,  is this working? Yeah, okay. The supporters,  
it is clear that supporters have only got one  thing on their minds at the moment. They are  
singing about Leipzig throughout. So how important  is it, and did you see out there today the fact  
that your players are able to put it to one side?  Does that performance show you that they are  
capable of doing that? Yes, exactly. And I think,  as I mentioned, two and a half weeks really feels  
for us so long because usually we have to play  five games between this. So we have now one, two,  
three more. Normally we have four, and today  five, but then it is so far away. And we are  
always talking about our standards. This is ours.  We always want to show our standard, because then  
we know we will have a good performance and it  means we will get enough points at the end of  
the season. That does not mean that you always  win, but I also felt that we had a very good  
performance at Liverpool when we lost 3-1. We did  not have a good performance against Bournemouth,  
but today it was a good performance. And I think,  for me, it feels maybe since the Fiorentina home  
game that everybody now is, we know we are coming  to the final stage of the season. This vibe  
started to create, and maybe right now the vibe  is here, around Selhurst, around the club, in the  
club, together with our fans, that everybody is  enjoying the football, everybody is enjoying the  
team, everybody is enjoying the club, everybody  is enjoying the fans. So everybody is enjoying  
himself and the whole situation we are in. And  this vibe, for me, started from this Fiorentina  
game. And then it is not a problem to be 2-1  down. It is not a problem for the fans, it is  
not a problem for the players, because everybody  has to believe we can strike back. And this is,  
I think, what the players, this group of players,  created again. I think it was a bit similar before  
the semi-final and final at Wembley. We played  Villa and Man City, but there was this same word,  
vibe, this belief, hey, we could get it done. And  this, for me, it feels like it is back again and  
we will need this until the 27th of May. And then  we will have two and a half great weeks together,  
and this is what it is all about. Last one is from  Bobby. Hi, Oliver. You targeted double figures  
for Ismaïla at the start of the season. Today he  became the first Crystal Palace player in 13 years  
to score 20 goals in a single season. Has how  far into double figures he has gone this season  
taken you by surprise? Yes, I was asked about it  before. I am a bit surprised that it is now 20,  
but I am pretty sure it will be more at the end of  the season because he is just doing so well. He is  
a threat, a permanent threat in every single game.  Even when he misses two, three chances every game,  
he has this confidence. He knows exactly how  we want to play. He knows exactly, not knowing,  
he feels the spaces where the ball will arrive. He  feels. He is always, it is great to watch him. And  
yeah, hopefully, no, definitely there will be  a few goals added to the 20 in these couple  
of years of working with him. What do you  think has improved most about his game?  
You know, I always, we did not find a special  button nobody found before. We did not make him  
quicker. We did not make him jump higher. I think,  and this is what we try with every single player,  
and not just me, with my staff together, to get  the best Ismaïla Sarr, the best Tyrick Mitchell,  
the best Jaydee Canvot, the best Dean Henderson  that he can be. And this is what, from day  
number one he came, he was not allowed to play for  Marseille, was not allowed to train with the team,  
six months without a game, no pre-season. But  from day number one we could see his attitude,  
we could see his talent. And then we integrated  him in the way we are playing. He knows exactly  
what we are doing in and out of possession. And  of course, then we are encouraging every single  
player to play with his strengths. So we do not,  of course we would like to see, but we do not ask  
Ismaïla to play six times one-touch football. But  we ask him to make the runs, occupying certain  
spaces where maybe he creates space for other  players. Let’s say this duo, this tandem with  
Daniel Muñoz, and he understands it now. They are  playing together for almost two years. Everybody,  
they know each other. He knows when the ball  is on the left side where he has to arrive,  
that he maybe gets the ball, for example with  his header, and all these situations, it is  
working and training with him. But it is  him, because he is listening, he is trying,  
and always trying to improve and not being  satisfied and saying, now, ah, it is fine,  
I have already scored 19 and it is a great season.  No, it is getting the 20th, getting the 21st,  
22nd. And this ambition he has in his mind  and the skills he has in his body, so that  
is why it was not so difficult for us. Okay,  thank you. Thanks a lot. See you in two days.
title: GLASNER: “IT’S NOT ROCKET SCIENCE FOOTBALL!”  Crystal Palace 2-2 Everton
